scope: Active v2 runtime and its tests; archived v1 retained separately. Documentation/formatting only.

S01.review: Repository decision register, Library checkpoint of 22 November 2026, and subsequent conversation corrections through assessment2.4.2. Later explicit decisions supersede earlier proposals.

S03.review: The four-family/twelve-tool choice is documented in the agreed record. The source is not treated as establishing any implementation coefficient.

S04.title: Ajzen — The theory of planned behavior: Frequently asked questions
S04.review: TPB provides the attitude/reference/control distinction. The implemented utility equation and parameter values are model choices. Author PDF lookup failed during this audit; no new claim of a full-text re-review is made.

S05.title: McFadden — Economic choices
S05.review: Cited by prior model documents as conceptual provenance. The keyed Gumbel scale and specific integration with TPB are engineering assumptions, not estimates extracted from this source.

S06.review: Ferraz/Finan2008 doi10.1162/qjec.2008.123.2.703; Enikolopov/Petrova/Sonin2018 doi10.1257/app.20160089; Vosoughi/Roy/Aral2018 doi10.1126/science.aap9559. Current audit relies on the decision record for their role, not a new empirical effect extraction.

S09.title: Pozsgai-Alvarez — Recalibrating anti-corruption assessment: theories of change in a multi-level approach
S09.review: The user explicitly selected inputs/outputs/policy-specific institutional outcomes/impact. The available published attachment was a one-page extract, and earlier records refer to an author draft. The model’s indicator formulas are operational proposals, not equations claimed verbatim from the chapter.

S10.title: Accepted assessment/reporting design, 23 November 2026
S10.review: Three stage measures, one-line interpretations linked to real events, policy-specific inherited/current/final conditions, baseline comparisons and equal activity windows were accepted and implemented in display2.4.2.

S11.title: Grimm et al. — The ODD Protocol for Describing Agent-Based and Other Simulation Models: A Second Update to Improve Clarity, Replication, and Structural Realism
S11.review: Primary journal article opened in this audit. The technical overview follows its seven-element structure, supplemented by implementation traceability and an evaluation/gap record. No ODD/TRACE certification is claimed.

entries.title: Purpose, scope and version identity
entries.narrative: Antarkya explores how people, organizations, expectations and anti-corruption reforms interact. It is an experimental society, not a forecasting service or a country ranking. Its 1,000 people are a scaled synthetic population. A month is a model update, not a claim that every activity takes a real month. The user selects a country, estimated starting conditions, reforms, initial resource mobilization and duration. The run compares that reform scenario with a society that retains its existing arrangements but receives no additional selected reform. Reading the result therefore requires both its institutional indicators and its conduct and burden measures.
entries.technical: Behavioral VERSION is 2.4.0 and the assessment display is 2.4.2 at audited commit 9ceb5ae38510f10d2211366406d150500a364a95. validate accepts duration 6–240 whole months, repetitions in {1,5,10,20}, a supported country, bounded numeric overrides, and distinct tool IDs with mobilization in [0,1]. Default country PER, duration 120, repetitions 1. Seeds are strings truncated to 100 characters. This documentation adds annotations and formatting, not a new behavior version. Profile, saved-result and observation schemas have separate identifiers.
entries.limitations: Passing implementation checks is not empirical validation. There is no national population expansion weight, endogenous GDP, complete legal system or calibrated policy forecast.

entries.title: People and principal roles
entries.narrative: Every dot is one person. Citizen, Business, Official and Politician describe a principal role rather than a moral character or an exclusive set of interests. Organizations contain those same people; adding organizations does not add another population. Small classes have enough representation for political and administrative interactions to occur. Role counts differ by country, but are model design choices rather than census shares. Individuals can retain multiple affiliations and support organizations outside their own category. A politician can lose office while remaining a politician; a change in a dot’s direction does not itself change anyone’s role.
entries.technical: createPopulation loops over config.countries[iso3].counts, creating exactly 1,000 IDs, with role indices 0,1,2,3. Counts are NGA [635,210,130,25], ZAF [610,220,145,25], IDN [625,220,130,25], IND [650,205,120,25], CHN [590,235,150,25], PER [630,210,135,25], BRA [600,230,145,25], USA [570,270,135,25], DEU [575,255,145,25], ITA [590,245,140,25]. IDs and people persist; employment transitions update role and organization membership without allocating a new ID. assertInvariants requires agents.length===1000.
entries.limitations: Country-informed composition has not been statistically calibrated; minimum representation disproportionately samples smaller roles.

entries.title: Heterogeneous starting profiles
entries.narrative: People begin with different resources, competencies, knowledge, expectations, affinities and motivational attachments. These are actual numerical fields used by the code. Country descriptors shift some starting conditions, while individual draws preserve variation within each role. None of those fields alone determines whether someone acts corruptly. The model then lets a preliminary year of activity create prior choices, experience and relationships. The visible initial society is consequently more developed than a collection of people with empty histories.
entries.technical: Agent initialization includes stable geography; org/memberships/support; nine motives; balance, income, living cost and six receipts; knowledge, disclosure completeness, control, descriptive conduct belief, normCorrupt, riskBelief, beliefs and sourceTrust; skill; decisions; last-24 meaningful opportunities; experience; office/eligibility; liabilities and financial pressure. Baseline knowledge .20+.55U, disclosure .15+.50U, control .25+.50U, skill U, norm clamp(−.45+.90U+(informality−50)/180,−1,1). Country shifts add (GE−50)/200 to control, (GE−50)/250 to knowledge, risk clamp(.10+.65RoL/100+centered noise,.05,.85), trust clamp(.15+.65GE/100). Psychological traits and their separate stream are specified in AK-ADP-01. Exact initialization expressions and numeric occurrences are indexed in the appendices.
entries.limitations: Generic heterogeneous priors are not surveys of personality, corruption tolerance, wealth or national inequality.

entries.title: Organizations, formal affiliation and affinity
entries.narrative: Eight civic organizations and twenty-four business organizations coexist with simplified public bodies, four regional service agencies and political organizations. A person’s primary workplace, formal membership and support are separate. Support can cross all four organizational categories. A civic organization may advance business interests, and an outlet’s organizational category does not guarantee independence. Leadership is held by a person already in the population. This allows personal motives and relationships to matter in organizational decisions without inventing an omniscient organizational will.
entries.technical: There are 8 civic and 24 business orgs, country-configured public-function nodes plus 4 service orgs, and 5 parties except CHN’s 3 political organizations. Primary workplace assignment is rank-biased using floor(U^1.3 * category size), with first members ensuring representation. All noncitizens have primary membership; citizens beyond category-seeding members join with .45 probability. Noncitizens may acquire extra civic membership with .20 probability; people in roles 0/1 may acquire party membership with .10 probability. Support combines .65 person/class affinity+.25 organization draw+.10 own-workplace term, clamped. Leaders are selected among matching-role members, falling back to available members. These assignments are not empirical probabilities.
entries.limitations: One primary fn field represents each public body; multiple tool capabilities do not amount to a complete multifunctional mandate model. Membership draws are not empirically calibrated.
entries.status: partially implemented; provisional parameters and explicit gaps

entries.title: Membership, recruitment and continuity of identity
entries.narrative: People can apply to join civic or political organizations, give notice to leave secondary affiliations, change public employment or transfer between agencies. These changes require decisions, costs, eligibility and processing time. They do not erase personal resources, beliefs or relationships. Formal membership remains distinct from sympathy. Recruitment uses actual candidates and their skills, with the possibility that connections override criteria or that review blocks the override. The resulting composition of an agency affects its work capacity.
entries.technical: organizations runs every six months. Due requests are processed at those reviews even though due=month+1, so effective waits can be six months. Leaving secondary membership costs .03 RU, joining .05 RU; officials cannot freely apply to civic/party membership through this routine, and public agency admission occurs through employment. Per-agent review probability .04; low-affinity secondary membership threshold .30. Service agencies replace one eligible official per review; 24 keyed citizen applicants are ranked by skill, with connected/fallback patronage candidates. Employment transitions preserve IDs, homes, finances, expectations and ties, move workplace coordinates and scale income by the role ratio (official 1.05 versus other .95). Annual rotation transfers at most one nonleader official per service agency to the next agency after a decision and .05 RU cost.
entries.limitations: No explicit retirement, birth/death, general private-sector hiring or residential relocation pipeline exists. Recruitment/turnover and leadership succession are simplified.
entries.status: partially implemented; provisional parameters and explicit gaps

entries.title: Stable geography and selective encounters
entries.narrative: Physical proximity affects whom people meet and how difficult access can be. Homes and workplaces remain relatively stable; agents do not wander randomly each month. Remote contact and organizational links allow influence across distance. The analytical integrity map is a separate display, so a dot moving toward a collaborator does not relocate its person in the geographic encounter model. Local and remote selection create opportunities, but do not determine agreement.
entries.technical: Homes cluster around five normalized centers; angle is uniform and radius sqrt(U)*.18, with coordinates clamped inside [.025,.975]. Organization locations vary around the same centers. nearest samples up to six unique candidates, uses remote probability .15, otherwise distance weight exp(−4d), and multiplies by .4+affinity+.8*relationship access. Contact is selected by −ln(U)/weight. Workplace distance is used for administrative and business-political contexts; home distance otherwise. Reporting cost additionally depends on geographic distance. No all-pairs encounter search is used.
entries.limitations: Coordinates are stylized, dimensionless locations, not a geographic reconstruction of national cities. Homes never relocate in the current engine.

entries.title: Nine interests and beneficiaries
entries.narrative: All roles can value social, economic and political consequences for themselves, their group and the public. The resulting nine positive weights differ between people. Economic motivation is therefore not synonymous with corruption, and public-oriented motivation is not proof of integrity. Each option specifies what its consequences are expected to mean for these beneficiaries. Experience can slowly change the weights, but never replaces the profile with a single honesty score.
entries.technical: Motive order is [social/self, social/group, social/public, economic/self, economic/group, economic/public, political/self, political/group, political/public]. Role-domain proportions are [.40,.35,.25], [.25,.50,.25], [.35,.35,.30], [.25,.30,.45]. Group beneficiary share=.30+.002(kinship−50); public=.30+.002(public/private separation−50); self is remainder. Independent gamma draws have shape 6*domainShare*beneficiaryShare and unit scale, then normalize to one. Positivity and unit sum are invariants. Long-run target is normalized originalWeight*exp(.35*salience), approached at .002/month. Group consequences are scenario-valued components, not a complete accounting of transfers to a named faction.
entries.limitations: The concentration 6, role shares, cultural mappings and motive drift are exploratory priors. Relevant-group utility is not fully resolved among multiple affiliations.

entries.title: Subjective choice, TPB and random utility
entries.narrative: A person evaluates the options they face using perceived consequences, reference expectations and perceived control. Their own interests determine which consequences matter most. The person chooses the highest evaluated option, including occasion-specific uncertainty. A choice is therefore probabilistic across occasions while still maximizing the person’s assessed utility on each occasion. Actual money, counterpart acceptance, legal scope and implementation constraints determine whether that intention can be carried out. A high subjective benefit does not guarantee success.
entries.technical: For option o, need=clamp((cost+.20)/max(.20,.90*expectedIncome+.15*balance),.5,2)+.50*financialPressure; multiply economic/self consequence by need. If corrupt, subtract riskBelief from economic/self, .30*riskBelief from social/self, and (.60 if office else .15)*riskBelief from political/self. Raw attitude=sum(w[k]*effect[k])−effort; raw norm=explicit option.norm else (corrupt?normCorrupt:−normCorrupt); raw control=explicit option.control else agent.control. Adaptive.decision applies only eligible component memories. Utility=adjusted attitude+.50*adjusted norm+.25*(2*adjusted control−1)−.20*ln(−ln(U)). Select strict greatest utility in option order. This hybrid is the model’s operational choice, not an equation estimated by Ajzen. Context mapping limits policy effects to appropriate decisions.
entries.limitations: Fixed consequence valuations, utility coefficients and Gumbel scale .20 are uncalibrated. Information uncertainty is not an explicit Bayesian model or a separately observed intention time series.

entries.title: Action-specific perceived consequences
entries.narrative: The model uses different choices for bribery, refusal, implementation, reporting, staffing, voting, publication and funding. Each choice supplies social, economic and political consequences for self, group and public beneficiaries. The same person can therefore make different decisions in different situations without changing class. Those consequence arrays describe subjective valuations; they are not themselves transfers, tax receipts or a measure of social welfare. The physical effects of an accepted action are recorded separately.
entries.technical: effects(social,economic,political) concatenates three length-3 arrays and rejects a vector not containing nine finite values. Explicit effects are supplied at each choose call, including ordinary lawful options, improper offers, acceptance, extortion/refusal, case delay/dismissal, implementation/selective/resist/redirect, priority/allocation, budget authorization, publication/sharing, joining/exiting and candidate choice. The generated Action catalogue includes every effects() call, its exact expressions, option name/context, reference code and source location. Need/risk/policy adjustments are applied later in choose; no array is silently converted into a realized money transfer.
entries.limitations: Not every context described in the original Word document has a distinct implemented initiator or action set; see the gap register.

entries.title: Encounters, corruption and victimization
entries.narrative: A bribe offer, counterpart acceptance, completed exchange and subsequent case are different events. A voluntary exchange normally requires both parties to cooperate and an actual transfer. Extortion is treated separately: the official’s improper demand is recorded, while the victim’s coerced payment does not make the victim a voluntary corrupt participant. This distinction matters for both the map and impact measures. A failed proposal is not credited as a completed exchange or automatically treated as an integrity choice by its proposer.
entries.technical: Monthly administrative demand probability is .45 for roles 0/1 and .12 for roles 2/3. Businesses have .10 probability of a politician contract contact; officeholding politicians have .20 probability of administrative pressure. Campaign citizen contact is .04 during the last six months before a nonappointment review. Stakes: contract gain 1.20, political-pressure .75, other .60; bribe .25 for contracts else .10+.15U. Successful contract diversion transfers up to .80 RU treasury→business organization; tax advantage transfers up to .15 treasury→person and increments foregoneRevenue. Related-party conflict review can block completion with probability .35*recordQuality*operative conflict capability. Extortion records the demand even if the victim refuses or cannot pay; paid victim burden is recorded separately. encounterCorruptActs counts completed voluntary encounters and extortion demands, not payments alone.
entries.limitations: The headline “completed corrupt encounters” includes extortion demands without successful payment. Administrative encounters themselves do not have a universal per-person or per-official time budget. Some original proactive politician/business and official/protection scenarios are absent.

entries.title: Meaningful choices and integrity recovery
entries.narrative: Shape reflects recorded conduct in the simulation, not public reputation or a diagnosis of permanent character. A circle is the default; a qualifying corrupt act produces a triangle. Recovery requires both elapsed time without a new qualifying act and repeated integrity-preserving action. Routine one-option duties and inactivity cannot manufacture recovery. Histories remain available after the icon changes, and other people’s beliefs need not change at the same time.
entries.technical: A meaningful choice is created only for an option set of length>1 containing at least one corrupt option. Its key includes month, context, action key and agent ID; the last 24 entries are retained. Lawful act() can complete only a still-open current-month keyed opportunity. Corrupt act() always records conduct, creating an entry if necessary. One corrupt act sets state=corrupt, lastCorrupt=current month and recoveryChoices=0. Recovery requires month−lastCorrupt>=6 and recoveryChoices>=3. Class activity uses current-role agents’ last-24 entries; its denominator includes attempted/uncompleted meaningful opportunities, not just successful acts. History does not fade with time alone.
entries.limitations: The criterion is an implemented option/record definition, not a complete legal adjudication. Map radial participation and icon recovery are different summaries of persistent history.

entries.title: Role expectations and institutionalized ease
entries.narrative: Repeated action is not automatically an institution. The mechanism requires an encountered reference to communicate approval or disapproval associated with a role. Stronger expectations can make a familiar lawful or corrupt practice easier to follow. Both directions are possible. Familiarity and approval remain different from objective guilt or public information; a relationship can facilitate cooperation without being corrupt.
entries.technical: A reference is relevant if it leads the counterpart’s organization or directional trust exceeds .45. For an encounter classed relevant, approval probability is clamp(.50+.40*Nref) for improper conduct and clamp(.50−.40*Nref) for lawful conduct. Observed approval/disapproval maps to a ±1 signal; the observing person’s normCorrupt moves .04 toward it, clamped [−1,1]. The corresponding organization/role practice strength moves .015 toward approval (0/1). Honest/corrupt practice priors each lie [.20,.60] and decay by .999/month. Familiarity multiplies certain decision efforts and service work by (1−.40*practice). The macro .65 threshold only emits a consolidation/erosion event; it is not an institution switch that changes the rules.
entries.limitations: Practical work reductions are implemented for routine services; many other reductions affect subjective effort rather than actual charged person-months. Reference transmission is not a complete multilayer institution model.
entries.status: partially implemented; provisional parameters and explicit gaps

entries.title: Individual receptiveness and numerical psychology
entries.narrative: Interventions encounter people with different openness, learning, retention, interests, knowledge and histories. Delivery, acceptance and strength are separate. A credible lesson may still be rejected; a receptive agent may receive a weak dose. These characteristics are stored and exported numerical profiles. They do not appear only in explanatory prose. Prior corrupt participation can affect receptiveness, and experience can slowly alter the characteristics themselves.
entries.technical: Initial openness, retention and learning are .20+.60*keyedU; baseline reporting safety .20+.60U. With public motive share P, economic-self E, honest reference J=(1−normCorrupt)/2, participation H, knowledge K and experienced trust T: alignment for risk=clamp(.45+.40E+.15K); for attitude/norm=clamp(.25+.35P+.30J−.20H); otherwise=clamp(.35+.35K+.30T). Uptake=clamp((.10+.55*openness+.20*alignment+.15*learning)*credibility). Conditional strength=clamp(.25+.45*learning+.30*alignment). Uptake and accepted magnitude use separate keyed uniforms. Feedback salience approaches experienced components at .08*credibility; feedback memory uses .10 adjustment. These traits are relative model variables, not psychometric measurements.
entries.limitations: Receptiveness coefficients and distributions are assumptions. There is no empirical individual personality calibration.

entries.title: Diminishing influence, reinforcement and wear-off
entries.narrative: A repeated intervention can reinforce earlier learning, but does not receive a fresh unrestricted persuasion allowance every time. Its available new influence declines, and retained influence fades unless reinforced. Direct ceilings differ by policy and decision element. This prevents repeated delivery from mechanically converting the entire society. Structural effects—such as actual pay or an accessible procedure—remain separate from direct persuasion.
entries.technical: For element ceiling M and n previous delivered component exposures, cap=M*max(.05,.70^n), incrementing n even if uptake is rejected. Accepted intensity I=U*individual strength*delivery quality. Gain=cap*I; restoration=.35*I*max(0,peak−level); level=min(M,level+gain+restoration). Duplicate event IDs are ignored within a bounded 32-event memory; lifetime counters remain. Monthly decay is exp(−ln(2)/(policyHalfLife*(.5+retention))). Cross-policy aggregate bounds are attitude .45, norm .45, lawful control .50, improper control .50, risk .60, knowledge .60, safety .60. Context and elementContext gates apply before decision adjustment. Education moves corrupt attitude toward min(−1,attitude); norm toward −1 for corrupt/+1 for lawful; lawful control toward one except silent/coerced/defer/resist options. Risk and safety use experience-specific targets, not automatic favorable directions.
entries.limitations: Delivered-but-rejected episodes still consume novelty. Bounded event memories do not provide permanent global deduplication after older IDs expire; generated event IDs normally remain unique.

entries.title: Evolving traits, motives, skill and income expectations
entries.narrative: History changes more than a person’s conduct icon. Service experiences and enacted choices make particular interests salient; actual receipts change expected lawful income; work can improve competence. Openness can fall with negative experience or entrenched participation. These are slow, bounded adjustments around an individual’s starting profile. They do not guarantee movement toward integrity or erase earlier experience after a job change.
entries.technical: Each month salience fades by .99 and feedback by .98. Motives approach normalized initialWeights*exp(.35*salience) at .002. Openness approaches base+.12*(2*trust−1)−.08*participation at .01/month, bounded within .15 of base and [0,1]. Learning and retention approach base+.15*feedback and base+.10*feedback at .005/month. Actual work improves skill by .003*time*(1−skill), capped at min(1,initialSkill+.20). Expected income moves toward actual gross lawful receipts at rate .05+.25*learning; decision need uses .90 of that expectation for net receipts. Supplements enter the same month’s receipt observation, avoiding a second low-income update.
entries.limitations: No independent age process, personality test, retirement or general skill attrition is simulated.

entries.title: Directional trust and useful relationships
entries.narrative: Membership, support and trust are different ways of being connected. A repeated useful interaction can strengthen an informal tie, including lawful cooperation. The two participants can trust one another differently. Coercion can weaken a relationship rather than being interpreted as mutual solidarity. Networks matter because they affect access, contact selection, reference influence and the opportunity to protect insiders; they are not a universal immunity score.
entries.technical: A link stores a,b, trustAB,trustBA,strength,count,corruptCount,born,last,lastKind. Access=clamp(.15 if shared membership + strength*directional trust); related means access>.12. Positive interactions can create a missing tie with probability .10 and initialize trust/strength .25/.10. Cooperation increments strength .03, forward trust .025, reverse .020; coercive/negative interaction decrements .06,.08,.04 respectively. Support toward the counterpart’s organization shifts +.015 or −.04. Each month .peers samples at most two sufficiently strong/trusted contacts using −ln(U)/(strength*trust). Initial ties derive from primary organizational members and are not automatically cross-class clusters.
entries.limitations: Relationships decay mainly through negative encounters, not a universal expiry timer. Strong access is a simplified protection opportunity; legal intervention still requires its actual process.

entries.title: Journalism, publication and funding leverage
entries.narrative: Media are functions of existing organizations and people, not a fifth class. Editors choose whether to publish under their own incentives, resources, independence and dependence on funders. Business support for civic organizations can create leverage without adding money to the reform implementation pool. Publication can prompt scrutiny, but does not establish wrongdoing. Corrections and contested claims coexist with case developments and final decisions.
entries.technical: publish selects a media outlet by keyed draw; publication requires .06 RU and a publish/withhold utility choice. Funding dependence uses active donor payments within 12 months, specifically linking a subject’s organization to the outlet, divided by estimated outlet income plus recent total funding. Every six months up to three business→civic funding opportunities offer .80 RU, subject to both donor/recipient choices and actual balances. Accepted funding lowers editorialIndependence by .015, bounded. Record visibility informs scoop access; strategic contested claims occur every nine months. Published linked allegations can refer a matter with .20 probability. A correction is attempted annually for a previously false story older than two months. Final decision stories carry announced decision and collected amount, not hidden guilt.
entries.limitations: No generated articles or complete social feed exist. Strategic misinformation content and correction discovery are simplified world-generator rules; editors do not explicitly optimize the falsity of content. Publication charges money but not a full shared newsroom time budget.
entries.status: partially implemented; provisional parameters and explicit gaps

entries.title: Access, sharing and the separation of belief from truth
entries.narrative: Agents act on what they encounter and accept, not on the analyst’s map or the simulation’s hidden truth. News exposure is limited by attention, geography and country media conditions. Credibility and personal learning traits affect belief change. Sharing can carry information beyond the outlet’s original audience. A dismissal does not automatically make an allegation false, and a correction influences only people who encounter it.
entries.technical: information considers at most the last 12 stories from three months and at most three directly accessed stories/person/month. Exposure=clamp((.03+.15*outletReach+.08*localProximity)*(.5+civilLiberties/100)). Credibility=sourceTrust*storyEvidence*(.25+.50*openness+.25*learning). Subject belief moves .15*credibility toward .70 for a claim or .15 for a correction; descriptive belief moves .04*credibility. Accepted correction raises sourceTrust .03; support for subject memberships moves −.025*credibility, or +.020 for correction. Sharing uses utility and at most two trusted peers, changing peer belief by .08*relationshipWeight*credibility. Descriptive conduct beliefs and normative reference expectations are separate fields. Public-case risk learning is deduplicated against personal adjudication.
entries.limitations: Beliefs are bounded scalar memories rather than Bayesian probabilities. General descriptive belief directly informs political reputation defaults; it is not a separate universal norm term in every decision.

entries.title: Money, lawful receipts and living needs
entries.narrative: Money persists across encounters and months. Wages, purchases, bribes, fines and reform disbursements move resources between accounts rather than creating an automatic social loss. Agents face living costs and can become cash-constrained. Public pay depends on the employer and public treasury; private activity and the treasury also receive simplified regular inflows from an outside account. These are normalized model resources, not a full national economy.
entries.technical: transfer clips finite requested amount to the source’s nonnegative balance. totalMoney includes outside, treasury, all persons, organizations and reform allocations. GDP scale g=clamp(sqrt(GDP-PPP/20000),.6,1.8); opening treasury=1800g and outside=10,000,000. Monthly outside→treasury=180g; public funding covers modeled official scheduled wages plus 3 RU; other org funding is 3+memberCount*(business1.25,party1.80,other.35), followed by overhead 1+.04members. Wage withholding=.10 of actual receipt. Needs=.90*initial income*(.65+.50 fixed U), with GDP scaling. Consumption pays .72 outside and .28 a sampled business. Financial pressure=.90old+.10*(1−actualConsumption/needs), clamped. Agent balance cannot be negative; unpaid ordinary needs do not become a separate debt stock.
entries.limitations: Outside is a large finite balancing account, not empirically modeled trade or taxation. GDP is fixed. Public transfers for a tax advantage are a stylized foregone-revenue mechanism, not a full tax-return model.

entries.title: Shared public staff capacity and priorities
entries.narrative: Public agencies cannot use the same staff time twice. Routine services, case work and reform implementation draw on a common capacity. Leaders’ priorities determine how much is reserved for each type of work, so a funded reform can still encounter a staffing bottleneck. Additional policies add competing demands. Competence and performed training affect capacity, while requests and files can remain unfinished.
entries.technical: Agency monthly capacity=matching-role staffCount*(.25+.40*organization skill+.35*mean staff skill). scheduleWork scores reform/routine/case options, exponentiates clamp(utility,−3,3)*2 and normalizes them into category time limits. Each task debits both remaining agency time and its relevant limit, recording reformUsed/routineUsed/caseUsed. Reform need=.60 if any active allocation; routine need=.50+serviceCount/memberCount for service agencies else .05; case need=.10+assignedOpenFiles/memberCount. Within categories priorities use utility difference between prioritize and defer. Cost, case readiness and money can prevent use even when category time remains. Invariant checks prevent category totals exceeding common capacity.
entries.limitations: There is no reusable shared-infrastructure asset deduplication across policy budgets, nor a general private-person time ledger. Reservations do not automatically rebalance unused time within the month.
entries.status: partially implemented; provisional parameters and explicit gaps

entries.title: Service queues and bounded experience feedback
entries.narrative: Administrative requests remain in queues until the relevant organization has money and reserved time. Preferential access can move a paid request ahead of others; its harm depends on actual scarcity rather than being assumed for every payment. Waiting and successful delivery change experienced trust, perceived lawful control and support. These updates are bounded once per person each month so multiple pending requests cannot multiply opinion change without limit.
entries.technical: Service priority is paid/preferential first, then arrival month and person ID. Work requirement is .025 PM service, .020 tax, .040 permit, multiplied by 1−.40*honest practice; money cost .015 RU. A completed task contributes satisfaction clamp(1−delay/6); an unfinished task contributes zero and increments personal waiting once. All a person’s monthly task satisfactions are averaged. Trust adjusts .08 toward satisfaction; control .025 toward .20+.70*satisfaction. Organizational support adjusts .04 times that organization’s request share; governing-party support .02 toward satisfaction. Service-contact count increments once at arrival. Aggregate serviceWait records completed delays, not a running sum for every still-pending request.
entries.limitations: Service units/costs are normalized assumptions. Formal denial and detailed service quality are not independently modeled.

entries.title: Country observations, proxies and uncertainty
entries.narrative: Ten country profiles provide dated background conditions and simplified inherited anti-corruption arrangements. Observations, proxies and assumptions have different evidential status. GDP describes the resource scale; governance descriptors inform bounded priors; political descriptors affect particular procedures and information channels. Unmeasured cultural conditions remain editable neutral assumptions. Selecting a country does not assign a measured corruption prevalence or a national moral character.
entries.technical: Country set NGA,ZAF,IDN,IND,CHN,PER,BRA,USA,DEU,ITA. profiles.js contains GDP PPP and WGI GE/RoL/regulatory-quality descriptors with source metadata; baseline.js adds FH 2026 civil liberties /60, FH2025 electoral-process /12 and participation /16 rescaled to percentages. Culture defaults are 50. Ordinary legal scope .75; ordinary capability .12+.65GE fraction plus ±.11 noise, bounded [.08,.90]. For mapped narrow OECD instruments scope=.40+.45*regulations fraction; capability=.75*ordinary+.25*(.15+.65*practice fraction) plus the same noise/bounds. Nigeria/India protection scope exceptions .40/.45 are explicit estimates. User overrides are validated and applied before warm-up. Generated country/data appendices retain every stored numeric value and URL.
entries.limitations: No new source verification or live national updates are implied by this code audit. Regulatory quality is a proxy for business conditions; cultural scores, class composition, allocations and most costs lack comparable empirical calibration.

entries.title: Functional architecture and jurisdiction
entries.narrative: Country differences are represented partly through which organizations perform prevention, investigation, audit, prosecution, decision, integrity and budget functions. A specialist organization does not automatically control the entire accountability chain. Civil recovery differs from criminal punishment, and political authority does not follow a competitive-election template in every country. These distinctions give the model institutional structure without pretending to reproduce every agency or legal rule.
entries.technical: eligibleTool gates public functions and, for pay/merit/rotation/declarations/conflicts, applicable individual roles. responsible routes civil matters to a civil body when present; China administrative decisions can use prevention; service-origin administrative cases can return to the employer. India complaints and Peru vote-buying use integrity intake. Covered NGA/IDN/CHN specialist matters may investigate through prevention. Criminal stage2 uses prosecution if available, otherwise investigation. Italy political-pressure conduct can take an administrative route. Service-origin intake uses jurisdiction, .12 PM/.01 RU and one-month handoff. Config nodes, names, political modes, cycles and relative first-review phases are enumerated in the generated configuration appendix.
entries.limitations: Routing is stylized, not a comprehensive current offence/jurisdiction map. Institutional independence, appointment protections and civil/criminal procedures are only partially represented.
entries.status: partially implemented; provisional parameters and explicit gaps

entries.title: A reconstructed pre-policy year
entries.narrative: The starting society includes a model-generated year of prior activity. This supplies past choices, service experience, ties, finances and unfinished cases before a new reform starts. “Inherited pending cases” therefore means files still open after those twelve preliminary months; it is not a national statistic. At adoption, new intervention-period counters begin while the unfinished work and people’s histories continue. Every comparison and repetition uses that same inherited society.
entries.technical: createInitial starts a raw population at month −12, sets eligibility and psychological clocks accordingly, and runs twelve ordinary monthly steps with no selected reforms under a dedicated pre-policy stream derived from country and initialSeed. It preserves cases/services, receipts, beliefs, history and networks; retains the latest three realized decisions; stores warm-up history/metrics in initialization; resets intervention-period metric/distribution counters and event feed; and resets initial organizational controllers. An active configuration cache avoids repeated warm-up. validateInitial reconstructs and checks expected fields, exact identities/counters, money and role counts. initialDifference ignores object-key ordering and tolerates only finite noninteger relative rounding <=1e−10; imported values are retained rather than replaced.
entries.limitations: Twelve months is a finite reconstruction, not a demonstrated equilibrium or estimated national backlog. Country-condition overrides change that reconstructed past; selecting different reforms or future event seeds does not.

entries.title: Keyed probability, paired worlds and exact replay
entries.narrative: Probability is implemented through reproducible draws. The same initial state and future-event seed reproduce the same sequence of random assessments and world outcomes. Fresh event seeds produce new future events while preserving the initial society. Reform and baseline use matching keyed draws where their situations correspond, reducing accidental noise in their comparison. Rendering and inspection do not consume those random draws.
entries.technical: draw returns (hash(String(seed)+"|"+key.join("|"))+.5)/2^32. The 32-bit hash uses FNV-style accumulation and integer mixing, not cryptographic security. Runtime keys include eventSeed|replicate, month, process and stable IDs; initialization uses distinct country/society, motive and psychological namespaces. Occasion-specific Gumbel draws are keyed by option name. The browser uses crypto.getRandomValues to obtain a new event identity unless exact replay is requested; continuing/stepping preserves the stream. Replicates append the replicate index. Legal coverage and diagnostic draws have separate fixed namespaces. Divergent endogenous events need not have true counterparts even when common shocks are paired.
entries.limitations: A 32-bit hash permits collisions and is not a security RNG or a proof of statistical independence. Determinism does not imply absence of probabilistic rules.

entries.title: Formal reform selection and legal scope
entries.narrative: Selecting a reform makes the formal reform active at the start. It does not simulate a preliminary political fight over the user’s choice. Existing institutions and capabilities remain underneath the reform. Legal coverage, operational capacity, installed reform delivery and personal learning are different things. Formal expansion can change eligibility while implementation remains weak; delivery does not follow merely from selecting a checkbox.
entries.technical: adopt creates a policy record with initialRate=rate=user mobilization, scope=originalScope=.85, formal=active, requirements, allocations, counters and reviews. Recipient organizations’ legal entry for that tool is set to scope. coverage returns eligible legal scope, constrained by policy.scope if selected. covered compares a fixed person/body/tool hash to that scope. operational is coverage*capability for aggregate use or a covered 0/1 gate*capability for a specified person. operatingPolicy additionally requires active formal status, installed allocation and last delivery at least currentMonth−1. expose requires that operating gate. Zero new funding preserves baseline capabilities but does not prevent the selected reform’s formal scope change.
entries.limitations: The common .85 scope and generic country/tool uplift are not a complete set of 120 independently calibrated reforms. Coverage-sensitive diagnostics can improve on formal adoption without demonstrating new delivery.

entries.title: Requirements, mobilization and initial allocation
entries.narrative: The user’s percentage sets the starting share of estimated additional resource requirements. It is not redrawn as a monthly success lottery. Public money must be available before it can be disbursed. Allocation follows a simplified country-specific central/local pattern and relevant institutional functions. Several reforms add their distinct setup and recurring requirements and compete for public resources. Outside stakeholder funding remains outside these implementation pools.
entries.technical: For eligible official+politician count n and GDP scale g, requirements are setup=(2+n*a_p)g, monthly=(1+n*b_p)g and time=1+n*c_p, with each tool’s [a,b,c] in config.costs. recipients selects function-eligible bodies; if both central and regional recipients exist, shares are centralShare/centralCount or (1−centralShare)/localCount; otherwise equal. Per month request=rate*(monthly+setup/3 while any recipient is uninstalled). Disbursement is transfer(treasury,allocation,request*share); requested and actually mobilized are distinct. Priority ordering is utility-based, not an independent random funding percentage. All cost tuples and allocation priors are reproduced in the generated parameter/configuration appendices.
entries.limitations: Allocation is not measured national budget distribution. Shared infrastructure setup is not deduplicated across policies; cost tuples and 100% requirements remain exploratory.

entries.title: Implementation, resistance and setup
entries.narrative: An implementing leader can implement, comply selectively, resist or redirect resources. Money, reserved time, coverage and organizational conditions constrain the result. Setup is a process: it must accumulate enough work and spending before new delivery becomes operative. A recipient can consequently remain unready for years. These decisions create the implementation gap rather than a universal policy-success probability.
entries.technical: Each allocation needs reqWork=requirement.time*share and reqMoney=requirement.monthly*share. If money is absent or available reform time<.05 PM, response is awaiting resources. Resistance spends no delivery work; redirection transfers up to .45*reqMoney to the leader and uses .05 PM, producing a conduct record. Fidelity=(.45 for selective else1)*coverage/originalScope. Available dose=min(1,availableTime/reqWork,allocationBalance/reqMoney)*fidelity; used=reqWork*dose, operating money=reqMoney*dose. Setup additionally spends up to setup*share/3*dose, accumulates dose/3 work and decrements its three-step delay on work attempts. Installation requires delay<=0, setupWork>=1 and at least .85 of estimated setup spending. Installed delivery raises capability .08*dose toward .98 and invokes only the selected tool’s actual mechanisms.
entries.limitations: Setup money and operating money can both be spent before installation. “Three months” is a minimum work-stage parameter, not a guaranteed completion time. Some prose channel descriptions are broader than actual exposure hooks.

entries.title: Resource reviews, narrowing and suspension
entries.narrative: Initial mobilization is chosen by the user, but later resource decisions belong to modeled actors. Reviews can increase, hold or decrease resources and can narrow formal scope. Those choices depend on assessed delivery, support, resistance, waiting, priorities and authorization. A reform can therefore stagnate, be selectively implemented or become suspended. Such trajectories are descriptions of recorded processes rather than preset success and failure states.
entries.technical: budgetReview runs every six months. Controller chooses increase/hold/decrease/narrow; budget leader chooses authorize/withhold, and a parliamentary coalition may require a second party leader’s approval. An authorized increase adds .10 to rate only if treasury>3*monthly requirements; decrease subtracts .10, clamped [0,1]. A later approved narrowing after at least one prior approved narrowing reduces scope .10, floor .20; at scope<=.25 a .25 draw can set formal=suspended. Feedback delivery=sum allocation work/(time requirement*max(1,month)), support=mean(.6 governing-party affinity+.4 experienced trust), resistance=share resist/redirect, waiting=mean personal wait/contact. No routine deposits are made by supporters.
entries.limitations: Exceptional event-triggered reviews, full repeal, explicit reinstatement and automatic trajectory classification are not implemented. Narrowing consent is simplified and not full national legislative procedure.

entries.title: Signals, reporting and case intake
entries.narrative: A modeled corrupt act need not become a case. A victim or witness must decide to report, an audit may detect a signal, or publication can produce a referral. These are limited processes. The same act does not become several files merely because it has several signals. Files can concern lawful conduct too, and opening one is not proof. Where a service jurisdiction is involved, local intake adds work and delay before the case proceeds.
entries.technical: Report cost=.18*(1−aggregate complaints access)+.03*distance to subject organization. Reporting uses subjective safety and reporting-specific knowledge; submission requires chosen report, cost<=.16 and cash>=cost. makeCase de-duplicates by recordId. Initial evidence=clamp(.25+.35*visibility+.30*(U−.5)); stage0 screening is due next month, with one more month if outside specialist coverage. Audit bodies process up to min(12,floor(available case time/.25)) sampled records from the last six months; each check costs .25 PM. True-signal threshold is operative oversight*(.35+.40*verified declarations+.25*target disclosure quality); lawful controls have .025 false-signal probability. Covered subjects may receive a .25-probability audit notice. Record source, jurisdiction, mandate, actors, reporter and route persist.
entries.limitations: A report’s viability threshold is .16 RU, not the earlier proposal’s .10. Detection sampling and reporting opportunity rates are assumptions, not observed national rates.

entries.title: Staged processing, discretion and evidence
entries.narrative: Case work requires a competent organization, staff time, money and elapsed process time. The controller can process, delay or dismiss, and connections change what those alternatives mean to the controller. Evidence develops through investigation; a case can close at several stages. Criminal prosecution, administrative remedy and civil recovery are distinct labels. The model can produce inappropriate adverse action as well as successful accountability, so detected cases and sanctions cannot be read as the true corruption rate.
entries.technical: Eligible case processing requires .55 PM at investigation, .25 at other stages and .04 RU; local intake additionally uses .12 PM/.01 RU. A related insider changes utility consequences of delay/dismissal; first corrupt obstruction can create conduct. Delay reschedules +2 months. Processing screening adds .08*operative agency capability; evidence<.32 screens out, otherwise investigation due+2. Investigation quality=max(operative oversight,operative agency)*(.50+.25*org skill+.25*staff skill); truth-conditioned evidence signal=.55+.40quality, lawful signal=.12+.40U. New evidence=.45old+.55signal. Next stage due+2; criminal prosecution requires evidence>=.40 and adds one month before decision. Adverse finding requires evidence>.55+.08*(1−decision-body skill). Controllers choose with subjective utility; evidence generation uses model truth as a world process, not information read by the controller’s choice function.
entries.limitations: Appeals, detailed legal proof rules, real judicial independence protections and all offence-specific national procedures are absent.

entries.title: Assessed liability, collection and accountability learning
entries.narrative: A financial order and actual collection are not the same. A person may owe money after the case closes, and future collections require both affordability and enforcement resources. Actual adjudication and accessed announcements can change perceived accountability costs, while duplicate messages are prevented from supplying repeated generic bonuses. Public communication announces what an authority decided rather than revealing hidden guilt.
entries.technical: Nominal liability is 2 RU, or 3 when the penalties reform is formally active, multiplied by operative collection capability/coverage. Initial payment is capped at .65 of current personal cash; unpaid remainder becomes a case/body-linked claim. Later collection costs .010 PM/.005 RU, preserves .50 month of living needs, and across all claims cannot exceed .15 of that month’s gross receipts. It reduces claims, increases treasury and case collections, but does not count a new sanction. Personal cost-belief update rate=.12+.12learning toward riskPrior+.35; public ordinary update=(.015+.025learning)*credibility toward prior+.15; bounded [.03,.95] and relative prior bands. Base risk relaxes .005/month toward prior. Case IDs are deduplicated in a 64-event memory. Communicated decisions use a recently operative tool risk pathway or the ordinary path, never both, and a personally experienced decision cannot add another public update.
entries.limitations: The risk score is relative expected cost, not a true probability of detection. Collection rules are generic assumptions and not claims about national garnishment law.

entries.title: Political support, officeholding and authority
entries.narrative: Political authority can change without replacing people or erasing their histories. Voters evaluate candidates using perceived conduct and affiliation, not the analyst’s conduct symbols. China uses a personnel-appointment mode rather than a competitive national multiparty election. Campaign opportunities occur before scheduled reviews. The actor controlling budget reviews is only one part of a simplified political system; the model is not an election forecast.
entries.technical: Configured modes are presidential, parliamentary or appointment; cycles are 48/60 months with scenario-specific first phases. Appointment considers up to eight eligible first-party politicians and uses incumbent utility. Other modes let all modeled persons choose an eligible party or abstain; options depend on candidate perceived conduct, affinity, representation and electoral-integrity-adjusted control. Party votes are aggregated; the top party supplies controller, and parliamentary coalitions add ranked parties until a majority of modeled votes. The former controller loses office, winner gains office; nextReview advances by cycle. A qualifying noncivil adverse case removes office and bars eligibility for six months. Other politicians are not automatically demoted to Citizen and histories/resources remain.
entries.limitations: All-person voting, simplified coalition formation, multiple office flags and relative calendars are scenario mechanisms rather than complete national electoral law. No legislature, campaign finance market or voter-demographic calibration is modeled.

entries.title: Collective feedback and consequential developments
entries.narrative: Collective change arises through stocks, queues, budgets, expectations, information and actor reactions. The model reports consequential developments rather than printing every routine transaction in the default feed. An emerging corrupt network requires repeated linked conduct and leverage, not simply dense social connections. National GDP does not rise because the simulated treasury accumulates cash. Implementation trajectories can be discussed from records, but are not assigned as hidden predetermined outcomes.
entries.technical: Every six months public delivery events can report treasury change>.25, service queue change>50, or pay-adequacy change>.20. Role-expectation events use .65 practice thresholds. Major public-disclosure milestones require evidence>=.60, a leader/officeholder, distinct reach>=150 for decisions or 300 for allegations/developments and a three-month system interval. Emerging capture-risk components use ties with >=3 corrupt collaborations, strength>.25 and activity within 12 months; require >=3 people, >=2 roles, an official/officeholder and >=3 recent relevant multi-actor abuses, and emit at most once per component key per 12 months. These events observe current processes; they do not directly add a generic corruption or economic shock.
entries.limitations: There is no separate GDP-growth equation, protest/organized-demand process, complete state-capture model or automatic five-trajectory classifier. Some macro variables are derived observations rather than causal state variables.
entries.status: partially implemented; provisional parameters and explicit gaps

entries.title: Anti-corruption body
entries.narrative: Organizational reform can strengthen screening/inquiry capability and staff skill, but implementation and each recipient’s setup still matter. Cases can arrive faster than they can progress. Effective exercise against powerful actors remains a substantive objective; the current headline is only a simplified capability diagnostic.
entries.technical: Installed work raises organization skill .008*dose and capability .08*dose toward .98. Actual staff work uses Adaptive.work. Screened subjects receive a risk exposure and reporters a reporting-control exposure only if the relevant allocation is operative. Investigation evidence can use agency capability. Direct ceilings risk .25 and reporting/case control .15; half-life 10.
entries.limitations: The diagnostic is not a stratified exercise of mandate under observed high-power opposition.

entries.title: Recruitment and promotion
entries.narrative: Merit reform changes actual review and staffing, not an honesty label assigned to incoming personnel. Candidates retain individual interests and histories; a skilled recruit can still act corruptly. Staffing affects agency competence and future public capacity.
entries.technical: Each six-month service vacancy uses a 24-candidate pool. Actual merit is a leader’s merit choice or review enforcement with probability operative merit*recordQuality. A blocked connection override does not become a completed patronage act. Appointment/induction exposures target norm .12 and control .15 only in recruitment, half-life 12. New report outcome=merit appointments/all appointments over 12 months.
entries.limitations: No general promotion ladder, protected selection committee or country-specific appointment pipeline is simulated.

entries.title: Staff rotation
entries.narrative: Transfers can change who works together and who controls a service function, but do not dissolve relationships automatically. The target is reduced closed-network continuity, rather than simply a larger transfer count.
entries.technical: Annual transfer opportunity is gated by operative rotation. A nonleader official can move to the next service agency after leader choice and .05 RU cost. Existing ties/home/identity persist; workplace and memberships change. Direct norm ceiling .10, integrity/case contexts, half-life 8. Continuity diagnostic checks same original leader, leader tie>.30 or a remaining member’s tie>.50 to original controller.
entries.limitations: It evaluates four service functions and direct ties, not comprehensive informal control or all high-risk public posts.

entries.title: Protection for reporting persons
entries.narrative: Protection must be encountered and delivered in time to matter. A reporter can learn from a remedy or from a failure; a statutory promise does not automatically remove fear. A coerced victim remains distinct from a corrupt participant.
entries.technical: Retaliation requires the perpetrator’s utility choice and >.15 RU. Actual protection requires >.25 remaining case time and a draw below operative protection, then uses .25 PM. Unprotected victim can lose up to .30 RU. Experience targets reporting safety1 or 0; successful protection may also improve lawful control. Direct control .25, safety .35, report/refuse contexts, half-life 8. Outcome=actual remedies/reported threats over 12 months; n=0 unavailable.
entries.limitations: Only modeled reported threats enter this realized denominator; missing complaints and unseen retaliation are not universal protection success.

entries.title: Asset, liability and gift declarations
entries.narrative: The model distinguishes the existence of a declaration obligation, record completeness, verification and useful scrutiny. Filing or an internal notice is not automatically public transparency. Financial records can assist a real audit and subsequent evidence process.
entries.technical: Installed work increases covered persons’ disclosure completeness by .04*dose*(1−completeness). Every six months communicated verification can create risk learning toward current belief+.10*completeness*(1−belief). Covered declarations enter audit detection through verification capability*completeness. Direct risk ceiling .15, integrity contexts, half-life 10. Output counts actual additional-reform verification notices; outcome is a record-based capability diagnostic.
entries.limitations: No itemized assets, gifts, liability forms or independent financial reconstruction are modeled.

entries.title: Conflict-of-interest disclosure and review
entries.narrative: Relationships do not automatically prove an improper conflict. The implemented safeguard can identify a related exchange and prevent its completion, with limited records and operative review. A prevented exchange and completed corrupt act remain different events.
entries.technical: Installed work increases recordQuality .03*dose*(1−quality). For a related bilateral exchange, review prevention probability=.35*recordQuality*operative conflict capability. Prevention generates actual contacts and can affect perceived norm .10 and improper control .25, in integrity/recruitment/implementation contexts, half-life 10. Output counts blocked exchanges once, rather than twice for the two contacted people.
entries.limitations: No comprehensive legal conflict taxonomy, recusal procedure or independent review appeal is simulated.

entries.title: Audits and investigations
entries.narrative: Scrutiny depends on actual time, accessible records and competent work. Greater detection can coexist with unchanged or lower corruption. Notices and published developments affect only people who encounter them; hidden audit truth does not directly educate every agent.
entries.technical: Audit detection uses record visibility, verified declarations and operative capability; investigation quality also depends on organizational/staff skill. Installed capability approaches .98 through delivered work. Communicated audit/inquiry risk ceiling .30, integrity contexts, half-life 8. Output counts completed investigation stages. Outcome remains the fixed-reference scrutiny/correction capability proxy.
entries.limitations: Actual completed correction is not separately tested in every diagnostic reference situation; independence and high-power opposition remain simplified.

entries.title: Remuneration and incentives
entries.narrative: Actual lawful receipts can reduce financial insecurity, but remuneration does not receive a generic honesty bonus. The relevant institutional objective is reliable adequate pay, and impact must still be assessed from conduct and burdens.
entries.technical: Installed reform operating funds pay covered officials supplements equal to operating cost*pay capability divided by eligible staff; remaining operating cost leaves the pool. Net output includes actual regular and supplemental public receipts after modeled 10% withholding. Outcome requires >=6 receipts and adequate net pay in at least 5 of6. Direct persuasion map is empty. Expected income and experienced financial pressure enter ordinary utility evaluation.
entries.limitations: Career incentives beyond simple role income/recruitment are not a full predictable promotion system.

entries.title: Financial penalties
entries.narrative: A credible penalty requires an appropriate decision, assessable liability and actual collection. Increasing a nominal amount alone need not change behavior. Outstanding obligations persist and can be collected later, subject to resources and affordability.
entries.technical: Formal active reform changes nominal2→3 RU liability; operative capability determines assessment/collection. Persistent claims and personal/public risk learning are detailed in AK-CAS-03. Direct risk ceiling .40, integrity contexts, half-life 8. Report outcome uses a12-month extortion cohort ending 6 months earlier, at least 20 violations, and observed collections per violation; legacy outcome uses its cumulative matured cohort.
entries.limitations: The reported realized ratio is not a calibrated probability of appropriate imposition times collectible amount, nor a complete violation-specific penalty schedule.

entries.title: Proactive disclosure
entries.narrative: Accessible information can make decisions more scrutinizable and supply journalists with material, but the model does not award a persuasion bonus merely for publishing. Disclosure quality and the actual information pathway should be read separately.
entries.technical: Installed work increases disclosureQuality .04*dose*(1−quality). Record visibility is disclosureQuality*(.4+.6*operative disclosure) where applicable, influencing detection/publication access. Direct persuasion map is empty. Output counts delivered public-record implementation PM, not fabricated government documents; outcome is a practical-transparency capability proxy.
entries.limitations: No itemized publication registry, statutory request process or complete test of document timeliness/accessibility is implemented.

entries.title: Reporting and complaints
entries.narrative: Access to an accountability channel differs from choosing to use it and from the case ultimately succeeding. Reporting depends on cost, geography, knowledge, safety, resources and a competent receiving process. Unresolved complaints are relevant here; the whole national service queue is not a universal complaints outcome.
entries.technical: Reporting cost and submission threshold are in AK-CAS-01. Encountered instructions require operative delivery; direct reporting control .30 and channel knowledge .20 apply only to report context, half-life 8. Actual submitted reports and complaint-source open files are observed. Outcome remains a fixed-reference intake/access proxy; the code does not execute100 independent real submissions for the diagnostic.
entries.limitations: It does not directly estimate the approved chapter-level share able to submit within an independently modeled 1-month/.10-RU requirement.

entries.title: Awareness and education
entries.narrative: Education is a delivered experience, not an automatic conversion rate. People may reject a message, retain different amounts, forget or need reinforcement. Knowledge, attitudes, perceived expectations and lawful control can respond differently. Direct attitude influence up to30% means a bounded change in a decision component, not a30-point reduction in national corruption.
entries.technical: For each operative recipient, teaching contact probability=.06*dose*operative education. Contact invokes separate uptake/magnitude draws with actual source trust and dose. Ceilings: attitude .30, norm .20, control .25, knowledge .35; integrity/report/refuse/recruit/implementation/case/retaliation contexts; half-life 6 adjusted by retention. Output counts delivered episodes regardless of uptake; outcome=100*mean usable knowledge across 1,000 agents. Conditions additionally show effective lawful reference approval, control and retained attitude influence.
entries.limitations: No role-specific question bank or empirically validated knowledge test exists. Repeated delivery counts contacts, not unique people or verified comprehension.

entries.title: Institutional indicators and fixed reference diagnostics
entries.narrative: A policy is assessed against its particular institutional objective. The model keeps that assessment distinct from activities and from corruption impact. Some indicators summarize actual processes, while others estimate capability from a fixed reference set. A fixed reference set means repeated evaluation uses the same comparison situations; it does not mean the score is frozen. Those capability scores remain proxies and should not be described as observed success rates.
entries.technical: Legacy diagnostic n is 100 for complaints, number of services for rotation and current official count for most other tools; education instead uses the exact mean of all agents’ usable knowledge. Fixed draws use Antarkya-fixed-diagnostic, societyDrawKey,tool,index. Backlog factor=1/(1+(serviceBacklog+caseBacklog)/memberCount); capacity=clamp((.5orgSkill+.5staffSkill)*(.4+.6backlogFactor)). Tool thresholds multiply coverage by their capability/record/verification formula, with score100*passed/n. The reporting layer replaces merit/protection with trailing 12-month observed ratios when n>0, penalties with its matured cohort, and otherwise uses legacy snapshot definitions. Legacy merit changes to observed cumulative appointments after 20; reporting merit does not. The measurement dictionary distinguish these two paths, denominators, units and missing values.
entries.limitations: No stratified high-/low-power standardized case execution, full lawful-control diagnostic or uncertainty interval is implemented. The minimum 20-observation rule is not universal: new merit/protection ratios use n>0 and show the count.
entries.status: partially implemented; provisional parameters and explicit gaps

entries.title: Package impact and paired comparison
entries.narrative: Impact asks how actual modeled conduct and consequences differ from the no-new-reform baseline. The main rate concerns corrupt encounters per relevant encounter, not detected cases or a sum of personal icons. Counts, victim payments, diversion, tax advantages, service delays and sanctions provide additional context. For a combination of policies, this is the package’s joint impact; a component’s individual causal contribution requires another experiment.
entries.technical: Rate=100*encounterCorruptActs/encounterOpportunities; zero denominator gives null. Paired difference is reformRate−baselineRate, in percentage points. For a trailing 12-month post-adoption window at t, subtract cumulative counters at s=max(0,t−12), then divide separately within each branch; never average unweighted monthly rates. Since-adoption uses s=0. The chart’s x-axis remains model months. Small differences use three decimals; nonzero magnitudes<.0005 use scientific notation rather than signed zero. Repetition statistics report mean/min/max paired differences across new event streams with identical initial society. They are simulation variation, not an empirical confidence interval. Macro consequences remain separately named quantities; a bribe/fine transfer is not automatically net social loss.
entries.limitations: No automatic leave-one-out attribution, full welfare account or comprehensive displacement estimator exists. Extortion demands count even when no payment completes.

entries.title: Policy-specific before/current/final monitoring
entries.narrative: The audit-facing assessment compares the inherited condition before formal adoption, the condition in the reform run and the matching baseline month. It reports actual activity over equal trailing-year windows rather than comparing a starting queue with a year of completed work. Policy-specific conditions replace universal case/service counts. The current column becomes final on completion, while the review control permits looking back without rerunning the model.
entries.technical: Simulation.monitor is an observation-only sidecar, separate from state and from the report(record,witness) complaint method. The pre-policy observation archive is cached outside starting state and recreated through initial-state validation. start is captured before adopt(); subsequent monthly samples store counts, each tool’s outcome/conditions/scope/n and impact counters. Activity counters receive actual process hooks, not policy-selection bonuses. Output window at t subtracts counters at max(earliestMonth,t−12), allowing negative inherited months. New reports retain −12..240 history and a bounded event index. Saved reporting schema is antarkya.reporting.v1. Existing rules-2.4 results without monitoring still load, show an explicit missing-history notice and require rerunning for the new panels.
entries.limitations: Some output categories are explicitly additional-reform contacts and have no modeled baseline delivery. General backlogs remain system context. Reporting does not empirically calibrate the observed processes.

entries.title: Interpretations and linked evidence
entries.narrative: Each stage has a short interpretation based on the measured result and, where available, references to actual tracked developments. There are predefined statements for greater or lesser delivery, missing delivery, improvement, deterioration, limited institutional change despite activity, and insufficient observations. Clicking a reference opens the record and highlights its actors. A chronology is not automatically described as a cause; the model does not invent anecdotes to make a result sound convincing.
entries.technical: interpret compares values using display-oriented tolerances: impact .0005 points, outcome .05 indicator units, output1e−8; indicator direction is explicit. Estimated diagnostics receive an estimated-capability prefix. eventsFor excludes future and initialization records, uses direct P-tool records and policy-relevant contextual cases, and ranks actual material setup/funding/suspension changes above routine reviews. Impact draws references from the whole package plus salient macro events, independently of selected policy. At most2 references appear inline, up to8 are available; the sidecar retains at most400 evidence records while protecting consequential per-policy candidates. Full completed logs are retained separately. All inserted text is escaped.
entries.limitations: Thresholds describe displayed precision, not statistical significance. Event ranking is explanatory selection, not causal identification or exhaustive evidence retrieval.

entries.title: Analytical integrity, affinity and cooperation map
entries.narrative: The map combines an integrity-related radial measure with affinity and cooperation. Colors identify principal role; shapes follow recorded conduct and recovery. Quadrants are reference directions, not membership boundaries. Someone can move toward agents from several other classes without changing role or physical home. The inner disc provides space for agents with no recent corrupt participation; distance within that disc is for legibility and networking, not a ranking of integrity.
entries.technical: Recent participation r=recentCorrupt/recentOpportunities. Positive r fixes integrity radius .54+.41sqrt(r); r=0 lies inside core .48. Initial healthy spacing is .035+.43sqrt(display hash). Role anchors are −3π/4,−π/4,π/4,3π/4; directional vectors combine a .20 class anchor with2*(affinity−.5) for every class. Eight deterministic local-grid passes use cell .032, minimum spacing .023, bounded repulsion and cooperative-neighbor attraction. Coercive links do not attract. Positive participation radius is reimposed after layout. Physical x/y are never changed. View retains up to2,400 ties; default drawing caps320, focus180, with role/link filters and pan/zoom. No baseline dot distribution is overlaid.
entries.limitations: Direction is a heuristic projection, not a geographic map, causal network embedding or literal degree of support for one adjacent quadrant.

entries.title: Influential actors and significant event feed
entries.narrative: Inspection emphasizes people with network centrality or practical control over organizations and budgets. The reason for highlighting them is visible. The default event list focuses on major developments, with a full-process option for closer review. Stable tracking IDs connect disclosures, case stages and decisions. An event can highlight its participants without giving those agents access to the analyst’s true conduct classifications.
entries.technical: Influence score is weighted degree plus 12 for the current budget controller plus 3 for organizational leadership; top 8 are selected each view. Detailed psychology/motives/decision traces are supplied for that subset; full final profiles are exported separately. emit assigns event-family ID, update number, month, kind, actors, status and salient flag. Default significant filter includes salient/macro/politics; live view sends the most recent 200 events and renders at most80 matching cards. Full completed events override that slice in worker results. Highlighting, filtering and inspection do not run choose() or draw world randomness.
entries.limitations: Weighted degree plus leverage is a heuristic, not betweenness or a full power theory. The live last200 slice can omit older major records; the assessment evidence index mitigates this separately.

entries.title: One-page interface, synchronized assessment and review
entries.narrative: Setup, simulation and assessment remain on one page. Setup edits prepare a different scenario rather than changing an active run. The assessment presents output, outcome and impact together; on narrow screens its three headlines remain visible and one larger stage chart is selected below. A common month marker connects the charts and condition table. Expanded implementation details remain available without overwhelming the primary results.
entries.technical: getConfig validates the active form; pending warns when draft setup differs from activeConfig. Output/outcome follow assessmentPolicy, while impact remains the package comparison. assessmentMonth=null follows latest; user review pins a month; starting/loading/resetting a run clears that pin. At completion latest becomes Final; earlier review remains explicitly labeled. Output is trailing 12 months including inherited history; impact window is user-selected post-adoption12 months or cumulative; outcome method is named. Condition table compares start, selected reform month and same baseline month. Latest live resource details explicitly name their own month if the chart is reviewing earlier conditions. CSS switches at850px; display code only consumes observations.
entries.limitations: Automated DOM harnesses are not an actual Android or browser layout/performance benchmark.

entries.title: Saving, loading, import validation and exports
entries.narrative: A saved scenario retains its setup and exact starting society. Completed results can be reviewed after loading without automatically starting a new run. Device storage can fail or be cleared, so JSON backup remains important. Results and profiles can also be exported for independent analysis. A saved completed result is not a resumable live execution checkpoint, and an old result does not acquire new measurements merely because the interface has been updated.
entries.technical: IndexedDB stores named scenarios, with localStorage fallback and remembered last setup. Payload schema antarkya.scenario.v2 includes modelVersion, profileVersion, creation time, validated config, initial and optional completed results. Import size limit 64 MiB; validation checks rules version, initial identity, finite/ranged data, person IDs, result structure, events, optional psychological profiles and optional monitoring schema. Old pre-2.4 starts require recreating settings. Existing 2.4 results without reporting remain readable with a missing-monitoring message. loadPayload terminates any worker, resets review state and renders without Run. JSON serializes full initial state and final results; CSV exports metrics, policy outcomes, agent summaries, events and decision/condition data according to each export handler. CSV guards leading formula characters in string cells.
entries.limitations: Import validation is not a proof that every saved completed outcome was produced honestly; files are not signed. Full in-flight checkpoint/resume and arbitrary cross-version migration are not implemented.

entries.title: Worker scheduling, repetitions and browser operation
entries.narrative: The browser runs the simulation in a worker so processing does not have to block interface controls.
